events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.17 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI service, so the fare moves with distance and any unexplained deviation flows straight into what the rider pays; the fare facts confirm a metered build-up (base $3.90, distance $34.84 for 24.7 km, time $12.96, platform $1.47 = $53.17) [F6]. The rider says the driver deviated without asking [F7] and the driver only says he followed his GPS [F8]; under RD-2 the metered branch refunds the extra km of every off-route segment that no exemption covers.

One off-route segment is recorded: 09:32–09:38, 2.96 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.00 km [F3]. Under RD-1 that segment constitutes a detour and is reviewed against RD-3, RD-4 and RD-5. My segment_findings mirror the trace: not exempt.

RD-3 does not apply: there was no in-app chat and no rider-named stop or edit-destination request, so the segment cannot be attributed to a passenger instruction [F7][F3]. RD-5 does not apply: there is no driver route proposal made before the deviation and no rider agreement, and the trace records no such evidence [F7][F3]. RD-4 does not exempt: the only traffic facts are speed-band 4 (30–39 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard, which is well above the band 1–2 congestion range and is at most corroborative, never a standalone exemption [F9][F10]; and no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F11]. Weather was fair, so no "reasonable cause" arises there either [F12].

Amount: the per-km rate is distance fare ÷ distance km = $34.84 ÷ 24.7 km = $1.41/km [F6], matching the $4.45 billed for 3.2 km in the fare breakdown [F4]; the rate is also the tariff used in the trace. Only the non-exempt segment's extra km are refunded: 2.96 km × $1.41/km = $4.1736 → $4.17 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The residual difference between the fare's 3.2 km excess and the segments' 2.96 km (≈0.25 km) is map-matching residue and is not refunded [F1][F3][RD-2][RD-1].

RD-6 does not trigger: the driver's 90-day profile shows 1 upheld dispute but route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case does not make him a "repeated" route offender and no account flag is warranted [F14][RD-6]. Not a safety case: no chat threat, no injury or dangerous-driving allegation, and no threat-tagged fact [F7][F8].

The refund is issued as a Ryde voucher and Ryde retains final discretion on refunds (this ruling is a recommendation) [RD-2][NS-7].

One stretch of the trip — about 3 km between 9:32 and 9:38 — took you off the best route with no instruction from you, no congestion, and no incident to explain it. That extra distance wasn't yours to pay for. We're refunding $4.17 as a Ryde voucher, which will be applied to your account. Thanks for flagging it — no further action is needed from you.

DRIVER: We've reviewed a fare dispute on one of your metered trips and it was upheld. The fare is based on distance, and the trace shows a roughly 3 km stretch off the best route with no rider instruction, no congestion, and no recorded incident. No exemption applied, so $4.17 of that distance is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. This is not treated as a safety matter and no action is being taken against your account. It's one case only and doesn't flag you as a repeat route issue — follow the app's navigation and you're fine.
